text:
Passive movement is joint motion produced entirely by an external force, such as a therapist, a machine, or the patient's other limb, while the patient's own muscles stay relaxed. It is used in physiotherapy to maintain range of motion, reduce stiffness, and assess joint mobility. The team note's description (resistance throughout, pushing past the normal limit) fits resisted or overpressure techniques, not passive movement, so I'd keep this definition.
